title: Let's play and give feedback on each other's AI-assisted games!
author: vanerb11
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'd love to check out what other developers are creating with the help of AI!

I thought it would be nice to organize a little feedback exchange. Share your game or demo in the comments, and I'll give it a try and leave you some honest feedback.

In return, I'd really appreciate it if you could check out my game too and share your thoughts!

**My game: Nova Collapse**  
[https://varkness-games.itch.io/nova-collapse](https://varkness-games.itch.io/nova-collapse)

It's a free space-themed Survivors-like where you control a growing star, collect upgrades, fight waves of enemies and decide when to trigger a supernova.

It's playable directly in your browser!

I'm happy to try different genres. Looking forward to discovering your projects and supporting fellow indie developers!

Let's help each other improve!

comments.author: Slickabaut
comments.body:
I will try yours from my computer in a bit once I’m on it. Your workflow sounds very close to mine, just a bunch of back in forth between Mai coding and re-iterating. I’d say AI is not very good with original idea, but I do think it helps build on ideas quite well, if I’m able to articulate what I’m thinking or direction I’m heading, it’s super good at helping structure those thoughts.

I have a few (4) I have been working on, but all are **mobile** **games**. They work on web and are all free, but I designed (and built) straight from my phone, for my phone. Also made with my kids, so none of these are really hardcore gaming…

\- [**Doomfall**](http://doomfall.io), my first, which I launched to App Store few weeks ago, is straight forward scorched earth like game. I spent a lot of time into a career mode, as I really liked Stat storylines, so almost of the fun I get is really from deep career runs… 

\- [Finalfive:](http://playfinalfive.com) a autobattle draft card game. You draft 5 cards, try and create synergies and see how far they can climb in the 100 floor gauntlet. Also has a creative mode where you can create characters, factions (5 heroes shared theme) or entire universe (450+ assets get swapped). You can share and add other universes. All are visual only, as the underlying cards are all the same so can still have daily, raids, heroic where all play same game (for leaderboards), still a lot of polish and visuals I’d like to improve (making the battles feel more immersive).

\- [breakfastball:](http://breakfastball.io) super early prototype of a hole in 1 challenge. Concept is one golf shot to make it, over progressively difficult obstacles (ie over a house or over a walking dinosaur or floating pirate ship) - this will be art heavy this I haven’t touched in a while… it’s also first attempt with something in 3d, but assume this will be most challenging to do.

\- sploot: one I’m most excited to work on, a dr Mario like puzzle game except the board is basically specimens, you drop in different kinds (color) to link like usual, the link causes explosions with goals to killing the bacteria inside. Each 10 levels the bacteria changes, some could be resistant, some grow rapidly, some have weak spots, etc. the specimens inside also move and have effects (duplicate, change colors of others, some move, so it’s like your playing a living board). another where core gameplay feels good, but now I need to think art and animation…

I used a combo of lovable, ChatGPT and Claude, connected to GitHub. I use lovable as my viewer, then primarily gpt for project management, notes, strategy, then i paste between the three of them what I want, get best plan, implement, test and refine, just an endless loop of testing / playing and refining as I go. 

https://i.redd.it/l8u6a1x09e2i1.jpeg

Thanks and lo look forward to checking out your game and will leave a subsequent feedback on it!

comments.author: Kitchen-Beautiful545
comments.body:
In a desktop Chrome test of the Sparrow run, the first level-up appeared at 9:35, with the Space-to-dodge hint dimmed behind the upgrade cards. After confirming Homing Missiles with Enter, the game resumed at 9:34 with the “MOVE!” warning over that same hint. I’d give the player a second of grace after the first draft, or keep that first dodge hint visible until they actually dash. The keyboard arrows and Enter worked well in the card menu.
